campaign.title: The Bell at Dusk
campaign.premise: A small keep is granted one season to become a refuge before a coalition of raiders, sappers, climbers, and siege beasts tests every defensive doctrine at once.
campaign.player_role: A newly appointed keeper who must choose a commander, open coherent packs, and turn a neglected fort into a place that can survive pressure.
campaign.regional_objective: Hold the keep long enough to evacuate nearby households or prove that the keep can become their permanent refuge.
campaign.invasion_force: The Ashen Host is not one army but several practical pressures: raiders seek the gate, sappers seek weak structures, climbers seek walls that only look secure, and siege beasts punish static layouts.

chapters.title: Open the Armory
chapters.summary: Choose a commander, open the first pack, and make the keep readable before the first warning bell.
chapters.player_question: What does this keep believe it is good at?

chapters.title: The First Bell
chapters.summary: The first invasion teaches one doctrine cleanly enough that the player can identify the counter before the wave ends.
chapters.player_question: Can my layout answer the threat I expected?

chapters.title: The Wrong Wall
chapters.summary: A combined doctrine exposes a weakness that cannot be solved by placing more of the same piece.
chapters.player_question: Which defensive idea failed, and what does the keep need instead?

chapters.title: The Refuge Bell
chapters.summary: The final wave forces a choice between holding the keep intact, preserving people through a scarred defense, or abandoning the walls with a plan.
chapters.player_question: Is the keep a fortress, a refuge, or a tool for buying time?

commanders.name: The Castellan
commanders.public_doctrine: A keep survives by making every room support the room beside it.
commanders.strength: Compact layered defense and strong recovery when the interior remains connected.
commanders.drawback: Repositioning is slow, so exposed outer rooms are expensive to save.
commanders.character_voice: Measured, architectural, and protective of the keep as a place rather than a weapon.

commanders.name: The Warden
commanders.public_doctrine: A defender who can move is worth more than a wall that cannot answer a new threat.
commanders.strength: Mobile response and strong recovery after a threat bypasses the first line.
commanders.drawback: The keep begins with fewer materials and needs exposed routes for rapid movement.
commanders.character_voice: Direct, impatient with static plans, and attentive to who is trapped behind the line.

commanders.name: The Quartermaster
commanders.public_doctrine: A reserve is useful only if it survives until the moment it is needed.
commanders.passive: The first pack each Preparation costs two fewer materials and a surviving Supply Cache releases two extra materials.
commanders.strength: Stretches pack, ammunition, health, and recovery reserves across a multi-wave defense.
commanders.drawback: Starts with the lowest materials and morale, so reserves that are exposed or unused never repay their cost.
commanders.character_voice: Exacting, practical, and always aware that every stored resource has already been promised.

commanders.name: The Marshal
commanders.public_doctrine: A posted specialist is strongest when the rest of the keep can still relieve the post.
commanders.passive: Assigned combat defenders deal one additional response damage.
commanders.strength: Turns distributed room assignments into a high-output command network.
commanders.drawback: Gains little before assignments and exposes concentrated value to command hunters.
commanders.character_voice: Calm, exact, and attentive to the human cost of holding every post.

packs.name: Pike Line
packs.purpose: Turn a narrow approach into a deliberate pressure point.
packs.limitation: Strong in corridors and weak when the enemy spreads across open yard.
packs.choice_text: Spend space to make one approach exceptionally readable.

packs.name: Field Engineers
packs.purpose: Make the keep recoverable after a structure is damaged.
packs.limitation: Consumes materials and creates a high-value support target.
packs.choice_text: Spend immediate strength on the ability to survive a later mistake.

packs.name: Firekeepers
packs.purpose: Deny open space and punish a predictable approach.
packs.limitation: Needs clear sightlines and can create unsafe movement lanes for friendly defenders.
packs.choice_text: Shape the battlefield rather than simply add another body.

packs.name: Scouts
packs.purpose: Reveal the invasion’s approach and improve response time.
packs.limitation: Information does not stop a breach unless the keep can act on it.
packs.choice_text: Spend a pack on knowing where the next problem will be.

packs.name: Runner Network
packs.purpose: Make open layouts and rapid relief viable.
packs.limitation: Fragile pieces lose value when lanes close or support is exposed.
packs.choice_text: Spend space on movement and a reserve instead of immediate stopping power.

packs.name: Fallback Convoy
packs.purpose: Hold a second line and spend one structure to save another.
packs.limitation: Provides less value before contact and consumes precious reserve space.
packs.choice_text: Reserve space and condition now so the keep can yield without collapsing.

packs.name: Crossbow Watch
packs.purpose: Pierce armored pressure from an elevated firing line.
packs.limitation: Upper-wall placement and finite ammunition make the firing line powerful but inflexible.
packs.choice_text: Spend wall space on a precise answer to armored advances.

packs.name: Bell Guard
packs.purpose: Preserve warning and response timing through disrupted sightlines.
packs.limitation: Both pieces are non-attacking and the link fails across floors or beyond range.
packs.choice_text: Spend support positions on a warning chain that keeps the forecast trustworthy.

packs.name: Shieldwall
packs.purpose: Build one resilient anchor and understand when protection will be bypassed.
packs.limitation: Static protection cannot stop a Shieldbreaker and leaves separated routes exposed.
packs.choice_text: Protect one line while retaining a direct answer or secondary defense.

packs.name: Road Wardens
packs.purpose: Delay one fast breakthrough and finish it before contact.
packs.limitation: Consumes two ground footprints and the obstacle deals no direct damage.
packs.choice_text: Buy exactly one tick on one authored approach instead of adding broad damage.

packs.name: Lantern Watch
packs.purpose: Reveal a concealed route for a disciplined upper firing line.
packs.limitation: Consumes two upper-wall footprints and the lantern deals no direct damage.
packs.choice_text: Spend wall space on visibility instead of accepting close interception risk.

packs.name: River Wardens
packs.purpose: Hold one bank without blocking Ash Ford's causeway.
packs.choice_text: Commit one bank while preserving the central crossing.

packs.name: Ferry Network
packs.purpose: Carry warning and ranged response between separated banks.
packs.limitation: Limited ammunition and modest stopping power.
packs.choice_text: Keep a mobile answer instead of duplicating a fixed line.

packs.name: Ridge Company
packs.purpose: Make one exposed Twinwatch post a disciplined command anchor.
packs.limitation: Concentrates value into a visible specialist.
packs.choice_text: Strengthen one post while preserving relief for the other.

packs.name: Mason Train
packs.purpose: Counter armored demolition with piercing tools and structural protection.
packs.limitation: Large short-range footprints cannot answer distant unit hunters.
packs.choice_text: Build one anti-siege pocket instead of broad coverage.

pieces.name: Crossbow Patrol
pieces.role: pierces armored targets from the upper wall

pieces.name: Watch Banner
pieces.role: coordinates one nearby ranged firing line

pieces.name: Ferry Scouts
pieces.role: answers pressure across a divided keep

rooms.name: Outer Wall
rooms.story_function: The visible promise that the keep can buy time.
rooms.visual_motif: Patched stone, colored pennants, and repair braces that show the wall’s history.

rooms.name: Inner Yard
rooms.story_function: The room that makes the keep adaptable or exposes how little room the player left.
rooms.visual_motif: Packed earth, movable carts, rain barrels, and clear lanes between buildings.

rooms.name: Gate
rooms.story_function: The obvious target that teaches concentration without making every wave a gate test.
rooms.visual_motif: Heavy timber, iron braces, a winch, and a bell rope visible from the yard.

rooms.name: Armory
rooms.story_function: The place where a doctrine becomes physical equipment.
rooms.visual_motif: Open racks, labeled bundles, and empty hooks that reveal what the keep lacks.

rooms.name: Workshop
rooms.story_function: A practical room that turns materials into another chance.
rooms.visual_motif: Braces, hammers, oil lamps, and chalk diagrams of weak joints.

rooms.name: Barracks
rooms.story_function: The room that makes defenders people with limits rather than permanent turrets.
rooms.visual_motif: Bunks, folded blankets, practice staves, and a board of changing assignments.

rooms.name: Supply Room
rooms.story_function: The room whose safety determines how long the keep can recover.
rooms.visual_motif: Stacked crates, ration tags, and a narrow door that makes inventory visible.

rooms.name: North Tower
rooms.story_function: A future space that becomes valuable only if the player invests in information.
rooms.visual_motif: Unfinished stairs, a wind gauge, and a view of the approach.

rooms.name: Old Chapel
rooms.story_function: A contested space where the keep decides whether it is a barracks, refuge, or monument.
rooms.visual_motif: Broken icon panels, stored blankets, and a bell whose rope has been replaced twice.

enemies.name: Raider
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player concentrate enough strength at the obvious entrance?

enemies.name: Sapper
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player protect support pieces rather than only the front wall?

enemies.name: Climber
enemies.teaching_question: Has the player left an interior response and clear movement space?

enemies.name: Siege Beast
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player preserve a recovery option when the enemy damages several pieces at once?

enemies.name: Shield Guard
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player distinguish ordinary damage from an armor-piercing firing line?

enemies.name: Ash Slinger
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player preserve reliable warning when sightlines fail?

enemies.name: Shieldbreaker
enemies.teaching_question: Did the player preserve a second line behind static protection?

enemies.name: Standard Cutter
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player protect a command anchor without abandoning the wider defense?

enemies.name: Outrider
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player delay or destroy a fast contact before it reaches the specialist line?

enemies.name: Gloam Knife
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player reveal the route or preserve a close-interception answer?

enemies.name: Battering Ram
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player pierce the engine or protect its declared room before impact?

enemies.name: Harrier
enemies.teaching_question: Can the player protect or replace the ammunition user nearest exhaustion?

events.title: Two Keys, One Keep
events.setup: The keep has two keys and two doctrines. One promises a connected defense; the other promises movement when the plan breaks.

choices.label: Give the keys to the Castellan.
choices.visible_result: The keep becomes a problem of adjacency, layers, and disciplined space.

choices.label: Give the keys to the Warden.
choices.visible_result: The keep becomes a problem of movement, signals, and timely intervention.

events.title: The Bell Has a Pattern
events.setup: A scout returns with a simple warning: the first attackers are not hidden, but they are testing whether the gate is the only place the keep knows how to defend.

choices.label: Concentrate the first line at the gate.
choices.visible_result: The obvious answer becomes strong, but the inner yard must remain usable.

choices.label: Leave a reserve in the inner yard.
choices.visible_result: The first line is less impressive, but a bypass will not be free.

choices.label: Use the forecast to delay the bell and finish one support piece.
choices.visible_result: Information buys a small amount of time, not a free defense.

events.title: The Wrong Wall
events.setup: The wall did not fail where the player expected. A supply room brace is split, one route is blocked, and the keep still has enough strength for one clear repair choice.

choices.label: Repair the supply room and preserve recovery.
choices.visible_result: The keep loses a little immediate strength but keeps its ability to recover.

choices.label: Move defenders through the yard and close the gap.
choices.visible_result: The Warden turns movement into time, but the yard becomes the next pressure point.

choices.label: Seal the damaged room and defend a smaller keep.
choices.visible_result: The perimeter shrinks, the interior becomes stronger, and nearby resources are lost.

events.title: Something Large at the Tree Line
events.setup: The final warning is not a number. It is the sound of trees breaking beyond the old road. The beast will damage whatever the keep has made most important.

choices.label: Lock the keep into a compact layered defense.
choices.visible_result: The keep becomes harder to enter and less able to protect the ground outside it.

choices.label: Clear lanes for a mobile response.
choices.visible_result: The keep gives up some construction strength to preserve movement and evacuation.

choices.label: Open the chapel as a refuge and prepare a controlled withdrawal.
choices.visible_result: The keep’s victory becomes measured by who reaches shelter, not only which walls remain.

endings.title: Stone With a Memory
endings.summary: The keep holds intact because its layout expressed one doctrine clearly and kept enough reserve to answer the final pressure.
endings.character_note: The Castellan or Warden names the one room that made the difference, making the victory teachable.

endings.title: The Open Yard
endings.summary: The keep is scarred, but its open lanes let defenders and civilians move before the walls became a trap.
endings.character_note: The report praises the space the player left empty on purpose.

endings.title: The Bell Carries
endings.summary: The keep does not remain fully defensible, but the refuge plan moves people and essential packs to a safer second position.
endings.character_note: The final bell is heard beyond the walls, where the next defense will be built.

endings.title: A Lesson in Empty Space
endings.summary: The keep collapses as a defensible position. The campaign report identifies which doctrine, room, or missing recovery option caused the failure and unlocks a shorter retry with that lesson visible.
endings.character_note: Neither commander calls the loss inevitable; the report names the choice that made it likely.
